answer: Staked identity bonds make sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock refundable collateral before it can act, and provable misbehavior burns that deposit. One forged identity is cheap, but a swarm needs a separate bond per address, so cost scales linearly with the fake population. Treat honest stake as a broad mesa the attacker must rebuild for every clone, while slashing is a mirror reflecting bad behavior straight back into lost funds. A thousand personas becomes a frozen tundra of locked capital no attacker can cheaply afford.
